read.thesis: Verizon's Q2 is a telecom demand-and-margin story, not a capital-cycle one: postpaid phone adds of 184k and FWA/fiber broadband adds of 348k, with capex held at $16.0–16.5bn and no capacity change.

capex.quote: Capital expenditures of $16.0 billion to $16.5 billion.

triggers.label: Broadband net adds 348k, +12.3% YoY
triggers.quote: Verizon delivered 348,000 broadband net additions in second-quarter 2026, a year-over-year increase of 12.3 percent.

triggers.label: Adjusted EPS guide raised to $4.99–5.04
triggers.quote: Adjusted EPS of $4.99 to $5.04, or year-over-year growth of 6.0 to 7.0 percent

guidance.metric: Mobility and broadband service revenue growth 2026
guidance.quote: Mobility and broadband service revenue growth for 2026 to be 2.5 to 3.0 percent
Adjusted EPS of $4.99 to $5.04, or year-over-year growth of 6.0 to 7.0 percent
Free cash flow growth of 9.0 to 10.0 percent year-over-year.
Cash flow from operations growth of approximately 2.0 to 4.0 percent year-over-year.
Capital expenditures of $16.0 billion to $16.5 billion.
Total retail postpaid phone net additions are expected to be in the upper half of the 750,000 to 1.0 million range

red_flags.label: Net unsecured debt up to $128.7bn from $110.1bn at year-end
red_flags.quote: net unsecured debt at the end of second-quarter 2026 was $128.7 billion

red_flags.label: Net income down 22.9% on special items
red_flags.quote: Consolidated net income was $3.9 billion, a 22.9 percent decrease year-over-year.
